utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's put an end to this today, and we'll continue next week with whatever you wanted to deal with. Mr. Stringer, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This relates to -- well, now that we're at the end of the second week of testimony and evidence for the general, it's occurred to us that perhaps given the number of documents that we expect the Praljak Defence is going to tender in IC lists after General Praljak completes his testimony, we wonder whether it might be more efficient for everyone for the Praljak Defence to submit IC lists perhaps on a rolling basis at the end of a week or so, rather than saving what might be hundreds of documents until the very end, because it's a burdensome process, I think, for everybody to put these IC lists together and to review them and comment, and ultimately for the Trial Chamber to rule. So we wanted to propose that perhaps we get this process underway on a weekly or some other periodic basis so that it's not all left for the end. And then my only other -- actually, this is more of an inquiry, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On your first item, Mr. Stringer's idea is quite interesting, I must say, because it's true that we have a wealth of documents. Does Mr. Praljak's Defence see a problem in giving us an IC list of all documents that were presented at the end of the week, with the exhibit numbers? Then we can compile an IC list; the Prosecution can then start working on it, maybe draft its objections if need be, rather than waiting to the very end of Mr. Praljak's testimony to have a staggering IC list? We'll probably have hundreds or thousands of documents in this huge IC list at the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you're suggesting is to change the rule that you prescribed in the instruction that you provided before and that we have all adhered to very closely. The Defence is absolutely willing and ready to accept another ruling. However, if you want to have a list submitted towards the end of each week, then I suggest that this should be done at the beginning of the week for the week before, because we have established our own work procedure, and it's not going to be easy to change it. We don't have enough staff. We are completing our list, we are checking and double-checking it on Saturday or even Sunday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you could do that at the beginning of the week. That way it would make everybody's work easier. The second point, please, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just an inquiry of the Praljak Defence, because we want to make sure that -- and maybe the other Defence teams as well. We want to make sure that we have all of our own documents ready for the cross-examination when that begins. Now that we're into -- we've gone through two weeks, I don't know where we are in terms of the amount of time that's been used, maybe about 15 hours. But I wanted to inquire of the Praljak Defence whether they're still sort of -- whether the pace that we're on is the one that's envisioned to continue. In other words, maybe they're moving faster and won't end up using all of the 36 hours, and it would be helpful if we had some idea where we're at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think we should burden the Judges with our requests. I think we can deal with that in a couple of minutes during a break. I'm sorry that my learned friend has not reached me first, but the mathematics are simple. There is our projection, there is official data on the number of hours, and we also adjust our estimates. I will gladly have a word with my learned friend outside of the courtroom. I don't think we should burden the Court's time with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think altogether you have about 20 hours left. Mr. Stringer wanted to know whether you were going to use up all of the remaining 20 hours, or whether you're going to cut it short. That was his question, but I don't think that you're able to answer right away. Now, one last thing. Next week, we're supposed to sit in the afternoon -- we were supposed to sit in the afternoon, but the Popovic Chamber will not sit in the morning. So if you don't see any problem to this, we could sit in the morning Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, rather than in the afternoon. So please take that into account. And we will reconvene on Monday at 2.15 p.m. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of May, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
